standard_prerequisites.name: The homotopy category of a full subcategory closed under the relevant operations embeds as a full triangulated subcategory, and a localization criterion characterizes when the localized category is equivalent to the target
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the construction of the functor on the derived category to the single requirement that every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from a complex in the subcategory.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every complex of modules admits a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex of flat modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the required resolution, since flat modules are torsion free with respect to a nonzerodivisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: A functor on the homotopy category of the subcategory that sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms factors through the localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the additive functor on the derived category whose value on a complex of torsion free modules is the shifted complex.

core_obligations: Let the target subcategory consist of the torsion free modules with respect to the nonzerodivisor and view its homotopy category as a full triangulated subcategory of the homotopy category of all modules, with the quasi-isomorphisms as the set of arrows to be inverted (proof lines 27542-27549).

Apply the localization criterion to the map from the localized homotopy category of the subcategory to the derived category, and reduce its being an equivalence to the statement that every complex of modules admits a quasi-isomorphism from a complex of torsion free modules (proof lines 27550-27559).

Prove that reduction: use the existence of a K-flat resolution by flat modules, which are torsion free with respect to the nonzerodivisor, to produce the required quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 27560-27563).

Define the shifted functor on the subcategory, note that the discussion at the start of the section already provides a well defined functor from the homotopy category of torsion free complexes to the derived category, and use the earlier statement that it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 27565-27573).

Conclude that the functor factors through the localized category, which is the derived category by the first step, and record that the resulting functor is additive and has the stated value on complexes of torsion free modules (proof lines 27573-27575).
proof_roadmap: Set up the subcategory of torsion free modules and invoke the localization criterion for its homotopy category (proof lines 27542-27559).
Produce a quasi-isomorphism onto any complex from a complex of flat, hence torsion free, modules (proof lines 27560-27563).
Check that the shifted construction sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and let it factor through the localization (proof lines 27565-27575).
difficulty_reason: The statement constructs the additive functor on the derived category that extends the shifted-complex construction, showing that on any object represented by a complex of torsion free modules it agrees with the shift of that complex, and warning in a footnote that the functor is not exact (statement lines 27531-27540). The proof is a localization argument: it isolates the subcategory of torsion free modules, invokes the localization criterion to reduce the construction to the existence of a resolution by torsion free complexes, obtains that from K-flat resolutions by flat modules, and then checks that the shifted construction on the subcategory sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms so that it factors through the localized category (proof lines 27542-27575). The reduction step is what makes the definition independent of the chosen representative. The counted span refers five times, three times to results of this chapter and twice to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
